subject: Inference runtime subprocessor decomposition & evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@meditrust.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: security@meditrust.com, procurement@meditrust.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference runtime supply-chain decomposition request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking the time last week. Meditrust's security review flagged a couple of runtime-level questions we need to close to proceed with procurement:

1) We need a decomposed list of runtime subprocessors (not just the high-level vendors) that the inference runtime relies on at request time (KV cache providers, prefix cache, telemetry collectors, model artifact storage, tokenization helpers, S3/CDN providers). For each subprocessor, please indicate:
   - role/purpose
   - data types processed (tokens, telemetry, customer identifiers, model artifacts)
   - residency (region) and whether keys are customer-controlled or Redwood-managed

2) Evidence: CAIQ/SIG relevant docs or an evidence stub for items marked as in-scope (SOC2 report pointers, onshore/offshore residency attestations, and KMS ownership notes).

We realize this is granular. Can you share a compact roster (CSV preferred) and an evidence delivery ETA? Procurement is tying the timeline to our PO dates.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Director, Security & Risk
Meditrust Health

--

(Attachment: meditrust-eval-checklist-2027.pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@meditrust.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference runtime supply-chain decomposition request

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can produce a compact CSV mapping of runtime subprocessors and a prioritized evidence bundle. Plan below:

- Deliverable 1 (by 2027-04-14 EOD): CSV roster with fields: subprocessor_name, role, data_types, residency, kms_owner, contractual_scope, sla_link.
- Deliverable 2 (by 2027-04-16 EOD): Evidence bundle (SOC2 link where available, onshore residency attestation, CAIQ pointers, and a short note for components without external attestations).
- Scope note: We will include transient/in-memory helpers (tokenizers, kv cache frontends) and CDN/storage used for model artifacts. We will not enumerate ephemeral ephemeral process IDs; instead we’ll enumerate providers and the functional components they serve.

Jonas, Marissa — looping you in for ownership on the CSV and the evidence pack. Jonas: can you pull the runtime dependency export and attach the initial roster? Marissa: can you scope the evidence items and flag anything that requires legal redlines?

Elena — is a narrowed CSV + evidence bundle sufficient for procurement to proceed, or do you need scanned originals for each attestation?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: request-summary-stub.txt)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference runtime supply-chain decomposition request

Irene / Elena —

Attached is the first-pass CSV export from the runtime inventory service (column headings included). I annotated rows that require additional provenance (marked NOTE: needs attestation). High level examples included:
- Redis KV cache (provider: CloudKV Inc.) — stores ephemeral tokenization keys; residency us-west; KMS: Redwood-managed (NOTE: needs attestation)
- Model artifact storage (provider: ObjectStoreX) — stores model binaries; residency eu-central & us-west; KMS: customer-key option available (we included both entries)
- Telemetry collector (provider: Telemetriq) — aggregates metrics and traces; processes telemetry only (no raw prompts), residency us-east (NOTE: requires CAIQ link)

I also included a small diagram of dependency boundaries (see kv-cache-deps-diagram.png). We'll convert 'NOTE' rows into evidence items for Deliverable 2.

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redwood-subproc-roster-20270411.csv; kv-cache-deps-diagram.png)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@meditrust.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@meditrust.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference runtime supply-chain decomposition request

Jonas — thank you, this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications that will help our security review: 

1) For providers marked NOTE: needs attestation — can you indicate whether Redwood can provide a written attestation (signed) versus a link to the vendor's SOC2/CAIQ? We prefer vendor-signed attestations where the vendor doesn't publish a public report.
2) For model artifact storage: confirm whether the customer-key option is available for all regions and if there are any functional differences (latency, cold-start behavior) when using customer-managed keys.

Procurement: is Meditrust okay with a staggered evidence delivery (CSV + high-priority attestations first, remainder within two weeks)?

Thanks,
Elena

--

Note: procurement@meditrust.com replies in-thread with approval for staggered delivery and asks for invoice contact, but I'm copying procurement separately for that thread.

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: elena.rossi@meditrust.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference runtime supply-chain decomposition request

Elena —

We can provide two classes of evidence:

A) Vendor-published reports/links (SOC2, CAIQ) — we’ll include URLs and the report summaries.
B) Redwood attestations — short signed letters confirming our control mapping for transitive components where vendor reports are unavailable. For CloudKV Inc. and Telemetriq I can initiate vendor outreach today; if a vendor-signed attestation is not obtainable within 5 business days we’ll supply a Redwood attestation and mark it as operational evidence.

On customer-key option: confirmed — the customer-managed key path is available in us-west and eu-central for ObjectStoreX. Operational caveats: using customer keys introduces a cold-start in some on-demand artifact pulls (~120-350ms), and cross-region replication requires explicit key sharing configuration. I’ll add that note to the evidence pack.

Next steps:
- Jonas: convert CSV NOTE rows into an evidence-to-do list and assign owners.
- Iren e: approve Redwood attestation template (I attached a draft).
- Elena: confirm whether scanned originals are necessary for any attestation or a signed PDF is sufficient.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redwood-attestation-draft.pdf)
